mechanism_narrative: A rise in housing starts indicates increased demand for housing, which can lead to higher economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of rising housing starts (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate below 4.5% signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment indicates a strong labor market, which can lead to higher economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of rising payroll employment (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates increased economic activity, which can lead to higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of rising industrial production (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in real GDP indicates increased economic growth, which can lead to higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days. This effect is amplified when housing starts are also rising.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of rising real GDP and housing starts (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the consumer price index indicates decreased inflation, which can lead to higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This effect is amplified when the federal funds rate is also low.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of low inflation and low federal funds rate (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate above 5% indicates a weakening labor market, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of high unemployment rate (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in retail sales indicates decreased consumer spending, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This effect is amplified when housing starts are also declining.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of low retail sales and declining housing starts (t-test p > 0.05).
